evidence: Matches RPC/REST/ZMQ label and modifies the internal HTTP server's handling of HEAD requests across RPC and REST endpoints.
rationale: Fixes HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection desynchronization and corruption behind connection-pooling reverse proxies. As noted in the description, transmitting bodies on HEAD responses violates RFC 9110, causing clients to leave unread body bytes on keep-alive sockets, which unauthenticated clients can trigger against reverse proxies like nginx.
